groundingDetail.original:
# Project Brief: Migrate Team Wiki to PlexiiWrite

## Goals  
- Transition our team’s collaborative knowledge base from the current wiki platform to PlexiiWrite to improve content visibility, searchability, and real-time collaboration.  
- Enhance team productivity by reducing time spent on content discovery and editing.  
- Ensure all existing documentation is preserved, accessible, and properly categorized in the new system.  
- Establish a standardized workflow for creating, reviewing, and publishing content.  

## Scope  
- Include migration of all active and archived wiki pages (excluding user-specific notes or private forums).  
- Implement role-based access controls to maintain security and editorial oversight.  
- Train team members on using PlexiiWrite’s features, including commenting, version history, and tagging.  
- Set up automated alerts and notifications for content updates and approvals.  
- Exclude non-content assets such as file attachments stored outside the wiki or external tools like Slack or Jira integrations.  

## Timeline  
- **Week 1–2**: Finalize content inventory, define migration criteria, and set up PlexiiWrite environment.  
- **Week 3–4**: Begin phased migration of content; validate accuracy and links.  
- **Week 5**: Conduct internal testing with a pilot group (10–15 team members).  
- **Week 6**: Full rollout to all teams with mandatory training sessions.  
- **Week 7**: Post-launch review and feedback collection.  

## Risks & Mitigation  
- **Data loss or corruption**: Mitigated by using a staged migration approach with backups and version control.  
- **User resistance to change**: Addressed through early engagement, clear communication, and hands-on training.  
- **Workflow delays during transition**: Minimized by defining clear ownership and timelines for each content type.  
- **Technical integration issues**: Resolved via pre-testing with PlexiiWrite’s API and compatibility checks.  

*Approved by: [Owner Name] | Date: [Date]*

# Onboarding Guide for New Support Agents – First Week

## Welcome and Overview

Welcome to the support team! This guide is designed to help you get up to speed during your first week. You’ll learn about key tools, standard processes, and how escalations are managed so you can provide consistent, effective support from day one.

Your first week will focus on understanding our systems, workflows, and escalation protocols. By the end of this period, you should be confident in handling common customer inquiries and know when and how to escalate issues.

---

## Week 1: Tools & Systems

### 1. Customer Support Platform (Zendesk)
- **Primary Tool**: Zendesk for ticket management, knowledge base access, and communication.
- **Key Features**:
  - Ticket creation and assignment
  - Customer history and conversation logs
  - Escalation routing rules
  - Internal team collaboration via comments
- **How to Use**:
  - Log in using your assigned credentials at [https://support.yourcompany.com](https://support.yourcompany.com).
  - Use the search bar to find existing solutions before responding.
  - Always tag tickets with relevant categories (e.g., Billing, Account Access, Technical Issue).

### 2. Knowledge Base (Internal Wiki)
- **Purpose**: Central repository of FAQs, troubleshooting steps, and product documentation.
- **Access**:
  - Navigate to “Knowledge Base” in Zendesk → “Internal Resources” tab.
  - Search by keyword or browse by topic (e.g., “Password Reset,” “Payment Failure”).
- **Best Practice**:
  - Check the knowledge base *before* replying to a ticket. This reduces repeat questions and improves resolution time.

### 3. CRM System (Salesforce)
- **Purpose**: Tracks customer interactions, account details, and service history.
- **Access**:
  - Open Salesforce via the Zendesk integration or directly at [https://salesforce.yourcompany.com](https://salesforce.yourcompany.com).
  - Use your support login credentials; ensure you have the correct profile (Support Agent).
- **Key Actions**:
  - Update customer records after resolving issues.
  - Note follow-up actions or pending tasks in the “Activity” tab.

### 4. Communication Tools
- **Slack**:
  - Join the #support-general channel for daily updates.
  - Use #onboarding and #urgent-escalation channels during high-priority events.
- **Email**:
  - All support emails are routed through Zendesk. Avoid sending direct emails to customers unless approved by a manager.

---

## How We Handle Escalations

Escalations occur when a customer issue cannot be resolved at the first level of support or when it involves complex technical, billing, or compliance concerns.

### Escalation Triggers
The following situations require escalation:
- Customer reports a critical system failure (e.g., service outage, data loss).
- Billing disputes that involve overcharges or policy violations.
- Technical issues requiring engineering input (e.g., app crashes, server errors).
- Legal or compliance risks (e.g., data privacy concerns).

### Escalation Process
1. **Identify the Issue**  
   Clearly document symptoms, steps taken by the customer, and any error messages in the ticket.

2. **Check for Existing Solutions**  
   Search the knowledge base to confirm no known fix exists.

3. **Assign to Escalation Queue**  
   In Zendesk, click “Escalate” under the ticket. Select the appropriate escalation level:
   - Level 1: Engineering Support (for technical bugs)
   - Level 2: Billing/Finance (for disputes or account issues)
   - Level 3: Legal or Compliance (for privacy or regulatory concerns)

4. **Notify the Escalation Manager**  
   A ticket will automatically be routed to your team lead or escalation manager within 5 minutes.  
   *Note*: You do not need to manually notify them—this is handled through system automation.

5. **Follow Up**  
   After escalation, respond to the customer with a clear message stating:
   - The issue has been escalated.
   - The expected resolution time (e.g., “We’re working with engineering to resolve this; you’ll hear from us by [timeframe].”)
   - A reference number for tracking.

---

## First Week Tasks & Checkpoints

| Day | Task |
|-----|------|
| Day 1 | Complete onboarding checklist, access all tools, attend intro meeting with team lead |
| Day 2 | Review 3 sample tickets and practice responses using knowledge base |
| Day 3 | Shadow a senior agent during a live support call (with permission) |
| Day 4 | Resolve 5 real tickets independently under supervision |
| Day 5 | Submit a short feedback form to your manager about what you learned |

---

## Support Best Practices

- Always respond within 1 hour of receiving a new ticket.
- Use clear, empathetic language—customers appreciate calm and transparency.
- Never make promises you can’t keep. If an issue is unresolved, say so directly.
- Document every step in the ticket for audit and learning purposes.

---

## Questions & Help

If you have any questions during your first week:
- Contact your onboarding manager: [manager.name@yourcompany.com](mailto:manager.name@yourcompany.com)
- Visit the support portal: [https://support.yourcompany.com/onboarding](https://support.yourcompany.com/onboarding)
- Attend the weekly team huddle at 10:00 AM every Monday (first week only)

You’re not expected to be fully independent on day one—your goal is to learn, observe, and grow. We’re here to support you every step of the way.

Welcome to the team! 🚀

Hi Team,

Excited to officially launch the Plexii Pulse project! This is a pivotal step in expanding our product capabilities and delivering deeper user insights through real-time analytics. Below are the key goals, timeline, and ownership responsibilities to ensure alignment and momentum.

Project Goals

  • Launch a real-time analytics dashboard that surfaces key metrics with sub-second updates.
  • Improve user engagement by enabling personalized insights via predictive behavior modeling.
  • Reduce time-to-insight from days to seconds across core customer touchpoints.

Key Timeline

  1. Week 1–2: Finalize MVP scope and data pipeline specs.
  2. Week 3–4: Build core dashboard UI and back-end ingestion layer.
  3. Week 5: Conduct internal testing and validate performance metrics.
  4. Week 6: User acceptance testing (UAT) with product & customer success teams.
  5. Week 7: Launch to beta users; collect feedback for iteration.
  6. Week 8: Full rollout to all customers with post-launch review.

Ownership

  • Product Strategy: Sarah Chen – owns vision, scope, and roadmap alignment.
  • Engineering Lead: Raj Patel – owns architecture, development, and performance.
  • UX/UI Design: Maya Lin – leads interface design and user flow validation.
  • Data & Analytics: David Kim – manages data pipelines, model accuracy, and reporting.
  • Customer Success: Elena Torres – provides feedback loop and validates real-world impact.

Please join the weekly sync on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM (all times in EST). I’ll be attending every session to support cross-functional alignment.

Let’s make this launch a success — together!

— Alex Rivera Product Lead, Plexii alex.rivera@plexii.com
Note: This email is intended for internal team communication only. No external sharing permitted.
